description: This bar chart, presented at a tilted angle, illustrates the "% point difference" across various neural network configurations. The horizontal category axis displays the configurations, with visible labels including "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU", alongside an unlabeled category on the far left. The vertical value axis is labeled "% point difference" and features a linear scale with a visible range from -0.1 to 0.2, marked by tick labels at intervals of 0.1. Grid lines extend parallel to the category axis from these tick marks. The data is represented by grouped bars, with each category containing a pair of bars: a light blue bar on the left and a dark blue bar on the right, both outlined in black. The chart lacks a legend to define the specific meaning of the light and dark blue colors. The bars extend either upwards (positive values) or downwards (negative values) from the 0.0 baseline. Approximate values vary across the groups; for instance, the tallest positive bar is the dark blue bar in the "hidden:[], linear" category, reaching approximately 0.28, while the most negative value is represented by the light blue bar in the leftmost unlabeled category, extending down to roughly -0.15. The categories do not appear to be sorted in a specific ascending or descending order based on the bar values, and no individual bars are uniquely emphasized beyond their standard color coding.
